extracted.intended_audience: researchers, students and general readers interested in digital culture, new media and internet memes
extracted.subtask_description: A scholarly book review assessing an academic monograph about Internet memes / digital culture, focusing on conceptual clarity, empirical illustration, and political relevance. Useful as guidance for evaluating or writing research-oriented books on memes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear definition of Internet memes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a comprehensive and clear definition of what Internet memes are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifman builds the concept of the Internet meme on Dawkins' idea of 'memes' and devotes chapters to arriving at a clear definition (notably Chapter 4). The review highlights that a strong, explicit definitional framework is a core merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview of memetics/history
rubrics_metrics.description: Offers a brief but satisfying overview of the field of 'memetics'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapters 1 and 2 summarize prior work in memetics, giving readers historical and theoretical context. Inclusion of concise background material helps situate contemporary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection between memetics and Web 2.0
rubrics_metrics.description: Connects the study of memes with modern digital culture and Web 2.0 dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 3 links classical memetic ideas to online participatory technologies, strengthening the theoretical basis for treating Internet memes as distinct phenomena in digital environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument that memes embody shared culture/participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Argues that Internet memes are more than just jokes and form a '(post)modern folklore' or shared culture of online participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central argumentative claim—that memes are indicators of an active digital culture and relevant to civic participation—should be clearly articulated and defended, as Shifman does (p.15). The review emphasizes taking memes seriously as cultural objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of real-life examples and illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrates and explains many real-life Internet memes to illustrate concepts and arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples such as 'David after Dentist' and inclusion of actual meme images (when possible) make the book accessible and grounded. The review notes that empirical illustration is a key strength, especially for readers new to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification/overview of meme genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides an overview and taxonomy of different meme genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 7 gives a detailed overview of genres (e.g., 'Lipsynch' videos, 'Reaction Photoshops'), each illustrated by examples. A useful book should categorize meme types and give genre-specific characteristics and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of drivers motivating users to remix/create memes
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains why certain digital content motivates users to create new versions or remixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6 discusses catalysts such as (sometimes unintentional) humour and representations of 'flawed' individuals; explaining motivational mechanisms helps account for why some content goes memetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of political memes and election campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Connects memes with political participation and electoral campaigning, showing how memes operate in political contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses examples like the 2008 US Presidential campaign to demonstrate persuasive and mobilizing roles of political memes, arguing for their relevance to political science as well as media studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nuanced account of professional versus amateur meme production
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledges that political and influential memes can be produced by semi-professionals as well as amateurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review notes examples such as the professionally-produced 'Yes We Can' video, indicating that effective analyses should avoid simplistic amateur/professional dichotomies and recognize mixed production sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument about peer-to-peer persuasiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlights that information from peers (friends, family) can be more persuasive than elite-produced messages, explaining why memes matter politically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifman's argument that peer-originated information increases persuasion underpins claims about memes' political potential; evaluations should assess evidence supporting this mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of grassroots mobilizing potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows how memes can function as grassroots mobilizers and tools for collective expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Occupy Wall Street 'We Are the 99 Percent' meme demonstrates how slogans/images can be adapted by users to express personal statements; strong work should document instances of grassroots uptake and affordances for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of research agenda and pointers for future work
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarizes main arguments and offers pointers for future research in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final chapter's short summary and research directions is noted; a valuable scholarly book should identify open questions and suggest avenues for further study, especially in an understudied area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and readability for non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Is comprehensive and easy-to-read, with many examples that help readers not familiar with the field to engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review praises Shifman's balance of theory and illustration, making the book suitable as an introduction. Clarity, approachable prose, and illustrative examples are criteria for broad accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual relevance across popular culture and political scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses both popular-culture memes and political memes, making it useful to scholars from multiple fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of its focus on varied meme types and political implications, the work should appeal to media studies and political communication researchers alike; cross-disciplinary relevance is highlighted as a strength.
